catapult.title: Right-of-Pivot Arm Strike Zone (x≈0.2–0.5 Default)
catapult.principle: Placing the red ball at x≈0.2–0.5 on the right half of the catapult arm creates a downward force that lifts the green ball in a rightward arc toward the basket. x=0.3 is the default starting point; x=0.2 at standard y reduces range ~1.3 units. Shifting x rightward (≥0.5) at standard-y positions risks diminishing returns.
catapult.when_to_apply: Default for all catapult strikes; start with x=0.3. At moderate elevated y (≈0.5), decreasing x below 0.3 increases range (see leftward-x skill). Do not exceed x≈0.5 without checking for diminishing returns.
catapult.example: Seed 43: x=0.3 y=-0.5 → green at x=3.10, success. Seed 48: x=0.3 y=0.3 → success. Seed 51: x=0.3 y=0.0 → success.

catapult.title: Low Drop (y≈−0.5 to 0.0) Maximizes Range; Binary-Search y First
catapult.principle: Drop height y is the primary range control: y≈−0.5 produces maximum range, y≈0.0 produces moderate range, y≈0.3–0.5 produces reduced range. A ±0.25 change in y at standard heights shifts landing x by 1.5–2.0 units. When standard y (≤0.0) is blocked, the operative range shifts to y=0.25–0.5, where lower y still produces more range.
catapult.when_to_apply: Default for all seeds; start at y=-0.5, then binary-search toward y=0.0 if overshooting. If gray_ball blocks all y≤0.0, shift to y=0.5 as first valid placement, then binary-search DOWN to y=0.3 or y=0.25 to increase range. Use y=-0.25 as first midpoint in standard regime.
catapult.example: Seed 49: y=-0.5 blocked, y=0.0→x=4.26 (overshoot), y=0.25→x=3.71, success. Seed 53: y=0.0→x=4.45, y=0.25→x=4.19, y=0.5→x=4.17 (y-dominant regime detected).

catapult.title: Overlap Fallback Sequence: y=-0.5 → y=0.0 → y=0.5 → Binary-Search y=0.3–0.5
catapult.principle: When y=-0.5 is blocked, try y=0.0, then y=0.5 with r=2.0. Once a valid placement at y=0.5 is confirmed, binary-search DOWNWARD within y=0.3–0.5 to fine-tune range, since lower y in this zone still increases range. Only escalate to y=1.0 if y=0.3 is also blocked or all y=0.3–0.5 attempts miss by more than 1 unit.
catapult.when_to_apply: When predict_first_contact returns invalid for y=-0.5; follow sequence y=0.0 → y=0.5 r=2.0 → binary-search y=0.3–0.5. Skip x=1.0 at y=1.0 always. For elevated green ball scenes (y≥-0.5), standard y slots may all be blocked and sequence starts at y=1.0.
catapult.example: Seed 48: y=-0.5/0.0 blocked → y=0.5 (x=2.37 undershoot) → y=0.3 (x=3.14, success). Seed 51: y=-0.5 blocked → y=0.0 valid (gap 0.21, success). Seed 52: y=-0.5/0.0 blocked → y=0.5 undershoot → bisect down.

catapult.title: Trace-then-Simulate: Gap Threshold, Bisect Chaotic Cliffs, Simulate Narrow Boundary
catapult.principle: At standard drop heights (y≤0.0), commit to simulate when gap is under 0.8 units. At elevated heights (y=0.25–0.5), commit at gap <0.5. When a chaotic cliff is detected in y=0.3–0.5, bisect to the midpoint rather than simulating immediately. After bisection has narrowed the cliff to Δy≤0.01 (minimum resolution), simulating the overshoot boundary IS valid—the green ball can contact the blue ball during its arc even if the final resting position overshoots.
catapult.when_to_apply: At y≤0.0: gap <0.8 → simulate. At y=0.25–0.5: gap <0.5 → simulate. If chaotic cliff: bisect first. Once Δy≤0.01 and no gap reduction is possible, simulate the overshoot side—arc contact is achievable at that boundary.
catapult.example: Seed 51: gap ~0.21 at y=0.0 → success. Seed 52: cliff at y=0.34/0.35 after full bisection → simulated y=0.34 (overshoot) → success via arc contact.

catapult.title: Seed-Dependent Scene Geometry Requires Per-Seed Calibration
catapult.principle: Arm height, pivot position, blue ball position, green ball starting position, and arm tilt vary meaningfully across seeds. If green ball starts at y≥-0.5 (elevated), standard low-y drops will be blocked, requiring elevated-y placements starting at y≈1.0–1.1. If blue ball is at y<-3.0, standard r=2.0 placements may produce too flat a trajectory.
catapult.when_to_apply: Always call describe_scene_geometry first; if green ball y≥-0.5, treat as elevated-arm seed requiring y≥1.0 placements. If first 2–3 standard placements show green going left, treat as non-standard geometry seed requiring extra calibration.
catapult.example: Seed 43: standard geometry → x=0.3 y=-0.5 → success in 4 steps. Seed 42: green at y=-0.38 (elevated), standard y blocked, needed y=1.0 x-sweep. Seed 53: blue ball at y=-3.02, needed x=0.1 at y=0.5.

catapult.title: Chaotic Trajectory Zones: Avoid Fine-Tuning in Sensitive Ranges
catapult.principle: Chaotic zones exist in both y and x dimensions where tiny parameter changes cause large trajectory swings: (1) y≈-0.15 to -0.25 at x=0.3; (2) y≈0.3–0.4 at r=2.0 in some seeds (Δy=0.1 → >1.9 range jump); (3) y≈1.05–1.1 at elevated arms; (4) x≈0.35–0.40 at y=0.75. When a chaotic cliff is detected, bisect methodically; the cliff boundary can be as narrow as Δy=0.01.
catapult.when_to_apply: When two consecutive traces with small Δ in x or y produce landing positions >1.5 units apart: for y-chaotic cliffs bisect (e.g., try y=0.35 between y=0.3 and y=0.4); for x-chaotic cliffs simulate overshoot side. Do not iterate further within the chaotic range without a clear bisection strategy.
catapult.example: Seed 44: y=0.5→x=4.50, y=0.7→x=-0.33 (y-cliff). Seed 52: y=0.3→x=4.23, y=0.4→x=2.71 (cliff); bisected to y=0.34/y=0.35 boundary; simulated y=0.34 → success.

catapult.title: Identical Range at Different x/r Signals y-Dominant Regime
catapult.principle: When trace_green_ball returns nearly identical green ball landing positions despite changing x or radius, the scene is in a y-dominant regime where drop height controls range. Stop iterating x or r and switch to y-binary-search or x-sweep at a different y level. If lower y is blocked, try x<0.3 at moderate elevated y (≈0.5) to escape the regime.
catapult.when_to_apply: When two consecutive traces with different x or r values produce landing positions within 0.2 units of each other; immediately switch to adjusting y. If y is blocked and regime persists at x=0.3, try x=0.1–0.2 at y=0.5 to break out.
catapult.example: Seed 44: x=0.3 and x=0.2 at r=2.0 both →x=4.50. Seed 47: x=0.3 y=0.5 and various r all gave x≈2.69. Seed 53: y=0.0→x=4.45, y=0.25→x=4.19, y=0.5→x=4.17 (plateau) → switched to x=0.1 → success.

catapult.title: x=0.2 Escape for Standard-y Chaotic Cliff (y≤0.0 Only)
catapult.principle: When y binary-search at standard heights (y≈-0.5 to 0.0) reveals that y=-0.5 and y=-0.25 produce identical overshooting landings but y=0.0 flips the green ball far left, shifting x from 0.3 to 0.2 at y=-0.5 reduces range by ~1.3 units. This escape is strictly for standard y (≤0.0): at elevated y (≈0.5), x=0.2 increases range (opposite effect).
catapult.when_to_apply: Only when standard-y (y≈-0.5 to 0.0) binary search hits chaotic cliff with both y=-0.5 and y=-0.25 overshooting identically but y=0.0 going far left. Do NOT apply at elevated y (≥0.5)—use leftward x-sweep there for the opposite (range-increasing) effect.

catapult.title: Elevated-y Fallback: x=2.0, r=1.5 at y=1.0–1.5 as Last Resort
catapult.principle: When the overlap fallback sequence reaches y≥1.0 and x-sweep at y=1.0 (0.3→0.5) still fails, escalate to x=2.0, r=1.5—not x=1.0 at y=1.0 (INVALID ACTION). At x=2.0, y=1.0, r=1.5, the red ball contacts the arm at a rightward strike point, sending green ball with full range. An alternative for elevated scenes is x=0.3, y=1.1, r=2.0 when x=0.3 y=1.0 is blocked by gray_ball.
catapult.when_to_apply: After exhausting x-sweep (0.3–0.5) at y=1.0 in elevated-arm seeds; use x=2.0 r=1.5 at y=1.0, then y=1.5 if still blocked. Skip x=1.0 at y=1.0 always.
catapult.example: Seed 36: x=2.0, y=1.0, r=1.5 → success. Seed 40: x=0.3, y=1.1, r=2.0 → green at x=4.32, success.

catapult.title: Leftward x Shift (<0.3) at Moderate Elevated y (≈0.5) Dramatically Increases Range
catapult.principle: At moderate elevated drop heights (y≈0.5), decreasing x below 0.3 dramatically increases green ball range—opposite to standard-y behavior. This occurs because at y=0.5 the arm contact geometry changes such that a more central strike delivers more angular momentum to the arm. When stuck in a y-dominant regime with insufficient or excessive range at x=0.3, try x=0.1–0.2 at y=0.5 before escalating to y=1.0.
catapult.when_to_apply: When y=0.5 with x=0.3 produces insufficient range AND lower y is blocked or chaotic; try x=0.2 (binary mid) then x=0.1 at y=0.5. Binary-search x between 0.1 and 0.3 to target blue ball position. Do NOT apply at y≥1.0.

catapult.description: Fine-tuning x or y in a chaotic zone when trajectory response is nonlinear.
catapult.why_it_happens: Agents assume monotonic response and keep incrementing when the system is actually sensitive/chaotic.
catapult.how_to_avoid: When two consecutive traces produce landing positions >1.5 units apart with small Δ, switch to bisection rather than linear search.

catapult.description: Using x=1.0 at y=1.0 in elevated-arm scenes.
catapult.why_it_happens: Agents choose an intermediate x value between 0.3 and 2.0 without checking validity.
catapult.how_to_avoid: Skip x=1.0 at y=1.0 always; go directly to x=2.0 r=1.5 as the elevated fallback.

catapult.description: Simulating the overshoot side of a y-chaotic cliff (y=0.3–0.5) without bisecting first.
catapult.why_it_happens: Agents see a near-target landing on overshoot trace and try to simulate without confirming the cliff boundary.
catapult.how_to_avoid: Always bisect the chaotic cliff first. Only simulate the overshoot boundary after bisection has narrowed to Δy≤0.01 and no further resolution is possible.

catapult.description: Placing the red ball at x>3 (far right of scene).
catapult.why_it_happens: Agents try to increase rightward strike force by moving the contact point further right.
catapult.how_to_avoid: Keep x within 0.1–0.5 for standard strikes; x=2.0 is maximum for elevated fallback.

catapult.description: Treating x=0.2 as a universal range-reducer regardless of drop height.
catapult.why_it_happens: Agents apply the x=0.2 escape learned at standard y to elevated y situations where x behavior is reversed.
catapult.how_to_avoid: x=0.2 reduces range only at y≤0.0. At elevated y (≈0.5), x=0.2 and x=0.1 INCREASE range—use this deliberately when in a low-range y-dominant regime.
